denominators.note: --retry=0 was mandatory: root vitest.config.ts sets retry: CI ? 3 : 1, which would otherwise let a flaky pass masquerade as green. Kernel regression count in this lane's own run (21 files/165 tests) is explicitly noted in CLOSURE_EVIDENCE.md as materially different from a ledger claim of 32 files/259 tests referenced in the task brief; the discrepancy is most likely scope (a wider audits-adjacent glob), not disagreement, but it was not reconciled and is reported as-is rather than silently resolved — see contradiction note in the final report.

knownConsequences.description: audit_domain_events is append-only by service-layer discipline only, NOT by a database trigger: a direct SQL UPDATE/DELETE is not blocked, proven by immutableTrail.test.ts mutating a row directly. The task brief's own wording ('immutable audit trail') reads as the stronger, database-enforced claim, which is not what exists today. This is a genuine gap relative to the task's named requirement, not a cosmetic finding.

transitionLifecycle (programService.ts:944-1002) performs a blind UPDATE with no optimistic-concurrency WHERE clause on the current state, so two concurrent transitions to DIFFERENT target states from the same source can both pass their gate checks against a stale read and the later UPDATE silently wins, while the earlier transition's audit-trail event still claims a state that no longer matches audit_programs.lifecycle_state. Lower severity than the exactly-once gap (already fixed by this lane's migration) because transitions are typically single-actor and low-frequency.

integratorChangeRequests.reason: transitionLifecycle has no optimistic-concurrency guard: blind UPDATE with no WHERE lifecycle_state = $current clause, so two concurrent transitions to different targets from the same source state can silently produce a stale-wins outcome, with the audit trail event of the losing transition surviving even though the state it claims no longer matches reality.
integratorChangeRequests.minimalHunk: add AND lifecycle_state = $current to the UPDATE's WHERE clause; if rowCount === 0, throw AuditStateError('stan programu zmienił się w międzyczasie'); requires auditRun to return the affected row count instead of discarding it
integratorChangeRequests.consumerTest: a new case in server/src/services/audits/__tests__/programService.test.ts (kernel, not this lane) — two concurrent transitionLifecycle calls to DIFFERENT targets from the same source state, asserting exactly one succeeds and the final lifecycle_state matches the winner

integratorChangeRequests.reason: No BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE trigger enforces append-only behaviour at the database layer; today's guarantee is service-layer discipline only (every write goes through recordAuditEvent, an INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING). A direct SQL statement, migration, or future new writer could mutate history undetected.
integratorChangeRequests.minimalHunk: add a BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger on audit_domain_events that raises an exception, or REVOKE UPDATE/DELETE from the application role
integratorChangeRequests.consumerTest: a negative test attempting a direct UPDATE/DELETE against the table and asserting it is rejected by the database, replacing today's test that documents the mutation succeeding

openItems: scripts/cleanup/verify-closure-lane.mjs grants its allowedNewRoots exemption only to files that are currently untracked (const isNew = !isTracked(file)), so a legitimately-placed new file starts being reported as a violation the moment it is committed. This lane's new directory server/src/services/auditProgramHandoff/__tests__/ matches the allowed pattern and is benign.

The two non-blocking integrator change requests above (optimistic-concurrency guard on transitionLifecycle; a real database-level immutability trigger for audit_domain_events) should be scheduled — they are real gaps relative to the task's own wording, just not urgent enough to block this evidence closure.

No browser/visual evidence exists for this task; the Audits UI surface itself was not exercised, only the service layer via direct calls and SQL fixtures (matching the kernel's own goldenFlow.e2e.test.ts pattern).
verdictRationale: G0/G1/G3 shared gates pass at this SHA. All 7 lifecycle stages are proven end to end with SELECT verification at every stage, cold readback, SoD (4/4 with exact denial messages), and tenant isolation (1/1) — 10/10 task tests plus 165/165 kernel regression (read-only). This is marked PARTIAL rather than DONE_CURRENT_SHA because the task's own investigation surfaced a genuine, non-cosmetic gap against its named requirement: 'immutable audit trail' is disclosed as service-layer discipline only, not database-enforced (no trigger blocks a direct UPDATE/DELETE) — that is precisely the guarantee this task was supposed to close, and it is not closed, only honestly characterized. A second gap (no optimistic-concurrency guard on transitionLifecycle) was also found and not fixed within this lane's one-migration budget. Both are recorded as non-blocking integrator change requests rather than shipped fixes. No browser/visual evidence exists for the Audits UI either. Given the guidance to prefer PARTIAL when torn, and that a disclosed-but-unfixed core guarantee gap is a real shortfall (not just missing polish), PARTIAL is the honest verdict.
